references.text: Here are mentioned Gideon's (Jerubbaal's) seventy sons, which Abimelek refers to in his speech to the citizens of Shechem.
Jotham repeats the reference to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal who were killed by Abimelek.
Laban uses the same expression 'my flesh and blood' (bone and flesh) toward Jacob, referring to kinship.
Judah uses a similar expression about Joseph as 'our flesh' to emphasize the blood bond between brothers.
The tribes of Israel come to David and say that they are his 'flesh and bone', the same expression Abimelek used.
David appeals to the loyalty of the tribe of Judah by reminding them that they are his 'brothers, flesh and bone'.
The continuation of Abimelek's speech where his mother's relatives speak in his favor in Shechem.
